chunks.title: Plugin Introduction and Overview
chunks.summary: The Battle Core plugin revamps the RPG Maker MZ battle engine to provide flexible Action Sequences, animated sideview enemies, damage styles, custom targeting, and extensive JavaScript notetags for complete battle customization.
chunks.content:
The Battle Core plugin revamps the battle engine provided by RPG Maker MZ to become more flexible, streamlined, and support a variety of features. The updated battle engine allows for custom Action Sequences, battle layout styles, and a lot of control over the battle mechanics, too.

Features include all (but not limited to) the following:

* Action Sequence Plugin Commands to give you full control over what happens during the course of a skill or item.
* Animated Sideview Battler support for enemies!
* Auto Battle options for party-wide and actor-only instances.
* Base Troop Events to quickly streamline events for all Troop events.
* Battle Command control to let you change which commands appear for actors.
* Battle Layout styles to change the way the battle scene looks.
* Casting animation support for skills.
* Critical Hit control over the success rate formula and damage multipliers.
* Custom target scopes added for skills and items.
* Damage formula control, including Damage Styles.
* Damage caps, both hard caps and soft caps.
* Damage traits such Armor Penetration/Reduction to bypass defenses.
* Elements & Status Menu Core support for traits.
* Multitude of JavaScript notetags and global Plugin Parameters to let you make a variety of effects across various instances during battle.
* Party Command window can be skipped/disabled entirely.
* Weather effects now show in battle.
* Streamlined Battle Log to remove redundant information and improve the flow of battle.
* Visual HP Gauges can be displayed above the heads of actors and/or enemies with a possible requirement for enemies to be defeated at least once first in order for them to show.

chunks.title: Plugin Requirements and Tier System
chunks.summary: This plugin is made for RPG Maker MZ only and is classified as a Tier 1 plugin. It must be placed after the VisuStella MZ Core Engine (Tier 0) in the Plugin Manager list to ensure compatibility.
chunks.content:
This plugin is made for RPG Maker MZ. This will not work in other iterations of RPG Maker.

------ Tier 1 ------

This plugin is a Tier 1 plugin. Place it under other plugins of lower tier value on your Plugin Manager list (ie: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5). This is to ensure that your plugins will have the best compatibility with the rest of the VisuStella MZ library.

Core-required plugins:
* This plugin requires the VisuStella MZ Core Engine plugin to work properly.
* Place this plugin underneath the VisuStella MZ Core Engine plugin in the plugin list.

chunks.title: Action Sequences Major Change
chunks.summary: Action sequences are now executed entirely by the Battle Log Window or through common events if using the Custom Action Sequence notetag. This replaces the default MZ mixed execution model.
chunks.content:
Action Sequences

- Action sequences are now done either entirely by the Battle Log Window or through common events if the <Custom Action Sequence> notetag is used.
In RPG Maker MZ by default, Action Sequences would be a mixture of using the Battle Log Window, the Battle Manager, and the Battle Scene, making it hard to fully grab control of the situation.

chunks.title: Damage Styles Overview
chunks.summary: Damage Styles are alternative damage calculation formulas that can be applied globally via Plugin Parameters or per-skill/item via notetag. Each style has unique properties for formula usage, stat scaling, and damage scaling.
chunks.content:
Damage Styles are a new feature added through the Battle Core plugin. When using the default RPG Maker MZ damage formula, the damage dealt is calculated based on the user's ATK and the target's DEF (or MAT and MDF for magical attacks). This is fine and dandy for most games, but some developers may want to utilize different damage formulas to better fit their game.

Here is a list of the Damage Styles that come with this plugin by default.
You can add in your own and even edit them to your liking.
Or just remove them if you want.

Style          Use Formula As   PH/MA Disparity   Stat Scale   Damage Scale
Standard       Formula          No                Varies       Varies
ArmorScaling   Formula          No                Varies       Varies
CT             Multiplier       Yes               Low          Normal
D4             Multiplier       No                High         Normal
DQ             Multiplier       No                Low          Low
Lo             Multiplier       Yes               Normal       Normal
Pokemon        Formula          No                Low          Normal
Minecraft      Formula          No                Low          Low
WoW            Formula          No                Low          Normal

Damage Styles can be modified within the Plugin Parameters in the individual Damage Styles section (should be there by default). They can also be applied to individual skills/items through the usage of a notetag:

<Damage Style>
  name: Style Name
</Damage Style>

This will use whichever style is found in the Plugin Parameters. They can be altered to have different names and properties.

chunks.title: HP Gauge-Related Notetags
chunks.summary: Notetags for controlling HP gauge display above enemy battlers, including visibility conditions, dimensions, colors, positioning, and scaling. Used for Enemy notetags.
chunks.content:
=== HP Gauge-Related Notetags ===

---

<Show HP Gauge: x>
- Used for: Enemy Notetags
- Replace 'x' with visibility condition for HP gauge.
- Default: false (gauge hidden)
- Conditions:
  - true - Always show
  - false - Always hide
  - defeat - Show after defeating at least once
  - reveal - Show after encountering at least once

<HP Gauge Width: x>
- Used for: Enemy Notetags
- Replace 'x' with gauge width in pixels
- Default: 120

<HP Gauge Height: x>
- Used for: Enemy Notetags
- Replace 'x' with gauge height in pixels
- Default: 12

<HP Gauge Color: css>
- Used for: Enemy Notetags
- Replace 'css' with CSS color value
- Applies to gauge fill color

<HP Gauge Back Color: css>
- Used for: Enemy Notetags
- Replace 'css' with CSS color value
- Applies to gauge background color

<HP Gauge Gauge X: y>
- Used for: Enemy Notetags
- Replace 'y' with X position offset
- Default: 0

<HP Gauge Gauge Y: y>
- Used for: Enemy Notetags
- Replace 'y' with Y position offset
- Default: 0

<HP Gauge Gauge S: y>
- Used for: Enemy Notetags
- Replace 'y' with scale percentage
- Default: 100

chunks.title: Action Sequence - Overview and Structure
chunks.summary: Action Sequences are plugin commands that control what happens during skill/item execution. They provide full control over animations, movements, effects, targeting, and timing through a comprehensive command set.
chunks.content:
Action Sequences are plugin commands that can be placed inside skills and items to control exactly what happens during the course of the skill/item's action. This includes but is not limited to: making the user move, perform attacks, wait for animations to finish, play sounds, display battle messages, apply damage, and more.

Action Sequences are executed through the use of Plugin Commands within the Skill/Item's effects list in the database. Each Plugin Command represents a specific action to be taken by the battle system.

Basic Structure:
1. ACTION START - Marks beginning of sequence
2. Action commands (movement, animations, etc.)
3. ACTION EFFECT - Applies damage/effects
4. Action commands (follow-up effects)
5. ACTION FINISH - Marks end of sequence

Action Sequences can be created through:
- Skill/Item database 'Effects' list
- <Custom Action Sequence> notetag for JavaScript-based sequences
- Base Troop events for common sequences

Timing Control:
- Most animation commands have built-in waits
- WAIT: command for manual timing
- ACTION EFFECT includes automatic damage timing

chunks.title: Action Sequence - Movement Commands
chunks.summary: Comprehensive movement command set for battler positioning including absolute movement, relative movement, random movement, jumps, floating, anchoring, and return to home position.
chunks.content:
=== Action Sequences - Movement ===

MOVE: To [target] [frames]
- Move battler to target's position
- Target options: user, target, last target, allies, foes, all, etc.
- Frames: duration of movement

MOVE: Away [target] [frames]
- Move battler away from target

MOVE: Toward [target] [frames]
- Move battler toward target

MOVE: Opposite [target] [frames]
- Move battler to opposite side of target

MOVE: Random [frames]
- Move to random position on screen

MOVE: Steps [frames], [distance]
- Move forward/backward by distance

JUMP: To [target] [frames], [height]
- Jump toward target with arc height

JUMP: Away [target] [frames], [height]
- Jump away from target

JUMP: Random [frames], [height]
- Jump to random position

FLOAT: Toggle [frames], [height]
- Toggle floating state
- Height: pixels above ground

ANCHOR: Set [x], [y]
- Set anchor point for positioning
- Affects movement and rotation

ANCHOR: Reset
- Reset anchor to default

RETURN: [frames]
- Return to home position

chunks.title: Animated Sideview Battler Notetags
chunks.summary: Notetags for enabling enemies to use sideview actor sprites with weapon support, motion customization, attack speed control, and positioning options.
chunks.content:
=== Animated Sideview Battler-Related Notetags ===

<Sideview Battler: filename>
- Used for: Enemy Notetags
- Sets sideview actor sprite for enemy
- Filename refers to img/sv_actors/ folder
- Enemy will behave like actor with full motion support

<Sideview Weapon: id>
- Used for: Enemy Notetags
- Sets primary weapon image
- ID refers to weapon index in img/system/
- Displayed during attack motions

<Sideview Weapon 2: id>
- Used for: Enemy Notetags
- Sets secondary weapon

<Sideview Weapon 3: id>
- Used for: Enemy Notetags
- Sets tertiary weapon

<Sideview Weapon 4: id>
- Used for: Enemy Notetags
- Sets quaternary weapon

<SV Motion: motion>
- Used for: Enemy Notetags
- Override default motion for enemy
- Motion options: walk, wait, chant, guard, damage, evade, attack, escape, victory, dead, sleep, abnormal

<SV Attack Speed: x>
- Used for: Enemy Notetags
- Attack animation speed multiplier
- Higher = faster animation
- Default: based on Plugin Parameters

chunks.title: Damage-Related Notetags
chunks.summary: Notetags for damage control including damage style selection, damage caps (hard and soft), armor penetration/reduction, healing caps, and custom JavaScript damage formulas.
chunks.content:
=== Damage-Related Notetags ===

<Damage Style>
  name: Style Name
</Damage Style>
- Used for: Skill, Item Notetags
- Applies damage calculation style
- Style name must match Plugin Parameter setting

<Damage Cap: x>
- Used for: Skill, Item Notetags
- Hard limit on damage dealt
- Value 'x' is maximum damage
- Healing also affected

<Soft Damage Cap: x, y>
- Used for: Skill, Item Notetags
- Soft limit with diminishing returns
- 'x': soft cap threshold
- 'y': percent of damage retained above cap

<Armor Pen: x>
- Used for: Skill, Item Notetags
- Ignores 'x' amount of target's DEF/defense
- Flat reduction bypass

<Armor Red: x>
- Used for: Skill, Item Notetags
- Reduces target's DEF by percentage
- 'x': percentage reduction

<Healing Cap: x>
- Used for: Skill, Item Notetags
- Maximum healing amount
- Only affects recovery, not damage

<Custom Damage>
  code
  damage formula code here
  code
</Custom Damage>
- Used for: Skill, Item Notetags
- JavaScript eval context
- Available: user, target, item, subject
- Return value becomes damage dealt

chunks.title: Plugin Parameters - Damage Settings
chunks.summary: Global damage configuration including Damage Styles list, critical hit rate and damage formulas, default damage caps, and armor penetration/reduction settings.
chunks.content:
=== Plugin Parameters: Damage Settings ===

These Plugin Parameters add a variety of things to how damage is handled in your game.

---

Damage Styles List
- Array of available damage styles
- Each style has properties:
  - Name: Display name
  - Formula: Damage calculation formula
  - Use Formula As: Formula or Multiplier
  - PH/MA Disparity: Physical/Magical difference
  - Stat Scale: Stat scaling behavior
  - Damage Scale: Damage scaling behavior

---

JS: Rate Formula
- JavaScript eval for critical hit rate
- Available: user, target, item
- Return value: critical rate (0-1)
- Default: LUK-based calculation

---

JS: Damage Formula
- JavaScript eval for critical damage
- Available: user, target, item, damage
- Return value: critical multiplier
- Default: 2.0 + LUK bonus

---

Normal Critical Multiplier
- Base critical damage multiplier
- Default: 2.0
- Modified by JS: Damage Formula

---

Maximum Damage
- Global hard cap for damage
- Default: 9999
- Can be overridden by notetags

---

Armor Penetration
- Flat defense bypass per instance
- Stacks with multiple sources

---

Armor Reduction
- Percentage defense reduction
- Applied before penetration
